entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Need a mat for the night, traveller?

variants.low: Mats are for paying guests.
variants.high: Welcome back, traveller. Your mat is dry.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: One dry mat remains.

variants.low: No mat tonight.
variants.high: I saved the dry one for you.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Your old mat is waiting, traveller.

variants.low: Your mat is taken.
variants.high: Your old mat is waiting. Sit, traveller.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: You will sleep in the mud.

variants.low: Mud is your bed.
variants.high: Mud tonight. The roof is for honest guests.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: I'm the bed-keeper. Beds and rope are my trade, sold from a chest inside the lodge, across the common from the Hist shrine. Travellers come in off the track or up from the landing and drink at the spring first. Then they find me. My hours are the late ones, while the lamp burns and the last lodgers hunt for a dry mat.

variants.low: Bed-keeper. I sell beds and rope from the lodge chest. Drink at the spring first, then come to me.
variants.high: Come in out of the dark. I'm the bed-keeper. The lodge chest holds my rope and my mats. Drink at the spring before anything else. Then find me. I'll point you to the driest mat there is.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: The village gives water to every traveller who climbs the path. The cup costs nothing. The rest I sell from the chest in the lodge, a mat for the night and rope by the arm-span. Those two feed the whole village, my own pot included.

variants.low: Water costs nothing here. Beds and rope cost what the village set. Take it or leave it.
variants.high: Water from the spring costs nothing, so drink all you like. The beds and the rope pay for the village's meals, mine too. Ask me about the rope lengths if you need a long one for the marsh.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: The spring families mend rope for me to sell. Tsono-Ra works behind the lodge and tests each length by pulling it, so I trust his rope before I trust my own eye. Vees-Wai tends the tree. Im-Moro pours at the stone lip. From the lodge step, I watch them all at their work.

variants.low: The spring families mend rope for me to sell. I deal with them. The rest of the village I leave to itself.
variants.high: The spring families mend rope for me to sell. Tsono-Ra's lengths are the best I stock. Vees-Wai tends the tree. Im-Moro pours at the stone lip. Walk over to the shrine and see them. They like a visitor.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Salt is in the spring now. I drink a cup before I lie down for the day. It bites more than it did. The tree over the pool droops. I see it from the lodge step. Giant wasps nest by the huts as well, so I tell travellers to walk the path and stay off the grass.

variants.low: Salt is in the spring. Giant wasps nest by the huts. Walk the path.
variants.high: Salt is in the spring now, a little more every week. I won't pretend otherwise to a friend. Giant wasps nest by the huts as well. Walk the path and carry a full jar for the road.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Helstrom lies south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. Fill a jar before you go. Both the road and the landing are a few steps from the spring.

variants.low: South-west, past Ux-Aneet, is Helstrom. The road and the landing both start near the spring.
variants.high: Helstrom lies south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. Fill a jar first, since the water costs nothing. The road and the landing both start a few steps from the spring, so choose whichever you trust.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Travellers bound for Helstrom sleep at the lodge. It's the village inn and I run it. The village agreed one price for a night, so I can't give one traveller a better price than the next. I take a fist of salt for a mat. Rope goes by the arm-span from the same chest. Spring water is free, so the beds and the rope pay for everything else.

variants.low: This is the inn. One price a night, agreed by the village, so don't ask me to bend it. Rope is sold here. Water is free.
variants.high: Travellers bound for Helstrom sleep here. You're welcome. The whole village agreed one price a night, a fist of salt, so every guest pays alike. Rope is sold here by the arm-span. The water is free. I'll tell you where the dry mats lie.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Argonians of the interior have their capital at Helstrom. The city grew up into a grove of Hist trees, so the houses stand among the trunks. A grove is a stand of those great trees close together. I rent a mat to nearly everyone bound there.

variants.low: Helstrom is the interior's capital. It grew into a grove of Hist trees. That's all I know.
variants.high: Argonians of the interior have their capital at Helstrom. The city grew up into a grove of Hist trees, with houses between the trunks. I rent a mat to nearly everyone bound there. Tell them Haj-Tei sent you and they'll give you the road news.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: The talk at the lodge is the salt. It has reached the spring. The families blame the salt works upstream for it. I'd guess the works wash their brine into the river and the river carries it down to us. I can't say how far upstream they stand.

variants.low: Salt has reached the spring. The families blame the salt works upstream. I won't swear to it.
variants.high: The talk at the lodge is the salt. It has reached the spring. The families blame the salt works upstream for it. I'd guess the brine washes down the river. If you pass the works, tell me what you see.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Mats for the night.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n1
entries.words: Who needs a mat?

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Fed yet?

variants.low: Not hungry. Move.
variants.high: Fed yet? Bowl is ready.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: The coals are low.

variants.low: Coals are low. Off.
variants.high: Coals are low. Take the warm side.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: You came back to my pot.

variants.low: Pot is mine.
variants.high: Back to my pot. Lid is off for you.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: You took from my pot, thief.

variants.low: Get away.
variants.high: Away, thief. Wasps can have you.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Eaten yet? This is the village over the spring. I cook at the fire stand before our hut and keep the pot lidded. The wasps come for it.

variants.low: Greenspring. The spring is there. I have a pot to watch.
variants.high: This is Greenspring, the village over the spring. I cook at the stand before our hut. Sit by the fire, the pot is nearly done.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: I cook at the fire stand before our hut. Spring water is free to any traveller. Beds and rope cost coin. The pot is hot by midday.

variants.low: I cook. Spring water is free. Beds and rope cost coin.
variants.high: I cook at the fire stand before our hut. Spring water is free to any traveller, so fill your skin. Beds and rope cost coin, ask the bed-keeper his price.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Vees-Wai is the tree-minder. He tends the Hist. Im-Moro keeps the spring. I cook for the families at the hut.

variants.low: Vees-Wai tends the Hist. Im-Moro keeps the spring. I cook.
variants.high: Vees-Wai is the tree-minder, he tends the Hist. Im-Moro keeps the spring. I cook for the families at the hut, so you will find me by the pot.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Salt comes down from the works upstream. The village blames them. Wasps nest close to my fire stand too, so the pot stays covered all day.

variants.low: Salt from the works upstream. Wasps at my stand. Mind yourself.
variants.high: Salt comes down from the works upstream, the village blames them. Wasps nest close to my stand, so keep clear of the thatch. Stay by the pot, I will watch the lid.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Helstrom is south-west of the spring. Walk past Ux-Aneet. The landing is below the huts if you want the river. Have you eaten first? Eat, then go.

variants.low: South-west, past Ux-Aneet. The landing is below the huts.
variants.high: Helstrom is south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. The landing is below the huts if you want the river. Take bread with you, the walk is long.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Have you eaten? We cook over the fire stands. The lodge jars get filled from the spring by us too. Mine is the stand before our hut.

variants.low: We cook over the stands. We fill the lodge jars. Nothing more.
variants.high: Have you eaten? We cook over the fire stands. We fill the lodge jars from the spring too. Mine is the stand before our hut, come by at midday.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Salt is getting into the spring. Talk at the lodge blames the works upstream. Mostly I hear about wasps, at my own pot.

variants.low: Salt in the spring. The works upstream, they say. Ask at the lodge.
variants.high: Salt is getting into the spring. Talk at the lodge blames the works upstream. I hear it all while I stir the pot, so come back at dusk.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Wasps at the pot.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2
entries.words: Keep that lid down.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Mind the coils, ojel.

variants.low: Mind the coils.
variants.high: Come and look at the coils, ojel.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Dark now. Work is done.

variants.low: No more talk tonight.
variants.high: Dark now, ojel. Sit a while.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: A good length today, ojel. Feel it.

variants.low: Not now, ojel.
variants.high: Pull on this one, ojel. It held.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Keep away from my coils.

variants.low: Go away now.
variants.high: Leave my coils alone.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: I mend rope behind the lodge, out of the sun, where the coils dry flat. The village sits round a spring with our Hist standing over it. The ground is firm here and the water is cold, so I am glad of the place.

variants.low: Rope, behind the lodge. The spring is round the corner with the Hist over it. Go and drink.
variants.high: I mend rope behind the lodge, out of the sun. Come and watch a coil dry if you like. The spring lies past the lodge with our Hist standing over it. Drink there first.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: The cup from the spring is free to any traveller. Beds and rope cost plenty. I mend the rope. Every length gets a hard pull before it goes to the lodge, because one that stretches is worth less than one that holds.

variants.low: The cup from the spring is free. Beds and rope are not.
variants.high: The cup from the spring is free to any traveller. Beds and rope cost plenty. I mend the rope. If you buy a length, ask for one of mine, because I pulled it hard and it held.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: My family mends rope for the bed-keeper to sell. Travellers talk to me only when they dispute the price. Then I tell them what the length will bear. They usually pay it.

variants.low: My family mends rope for the bed-keeper to sell. The price is his to name.
variants.high: My family mends rope for the bed-keeper to sell. I am out behind the lodge from first light. Come by if the price troubles you. I will say what the length will bear.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Salt is in the spring now, a little more each week. I taste it in the cup at dusk. Wasps nest too close to our fire stand as well, so I carry my coils wide of the thatch.

variants.low: Salt is in the spring. Wasps nest by our fire stand. Mind the thatch.
variants.high: Salt is in the spring, more each week. Taste a cup at dusk and you will know. The wasps nest too close to our fire stand, so walk wide of the thatch, traveller.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Helstrom is south-west of the spring. Walk through the village of Ux-Aneet. The road continues beyond it. The river landing is below the huts if you want the boats.

variants.low: Helstrom is south-west of the spring, past the village of Ux-Aneet.
variants.high: Helstrom is south-west of the spring, past the village of Ux-Aneet. The road is a short walk from here. Drink before you leave. The water costs you nothing.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: We cook at the fire stands before the huts. The lodge jars are filled from the spring each morning. My part is the rope. Mee-Sei does better with a pot than I do.

variants.low: We cook at the fire stands and fill the lodge jars. I do the rope.
variants.high: We cook at the fire stands before the huts. The lodge jars are filled from the spring each morning. My part is rope. Mee-Sei at the fire stand will feed you.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Ojel is our word for outsiders. It carries no insult, so say it freely. Those hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist, the great tree that speaks to us. The An-Xileel made a slur for them. I will not say it.

variants.low: Ojel means outsider. It is not an insult. Those hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist.
variants.high: Ojel is our word for outsiders. It carries no insult, so say it freely. Those hatched outside Black Marsh cannot hear the Hist, the tree that speaks to us. There is a slur for them. I will not say it. You will hear it from other mouths. Leave it there.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: At the lodge, they argue over who will take the next load down to Helstrom. The other talk is salt reaching our spring. I hear both from behind the lodge while I pull on my coils.

variants.low: They argue at the lodge over who hauls the next load to Helstrom. Salt in our spring is the other talk.
variants.high: At the lodge, they argue over who hauls the next load to Helstrom. The other talk is salt in our spring. I hear it all behind the lodge, so come and ask me what they said.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Step round the coils.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-2
entries.words: Pull it again.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Six jars filled, four to go.

variants.low: Jars first. Then talk.
variants.high: Seven filled already, traveller. Come and drink.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Asleep. Try me when the jars are out.

variants.low: Asleep. Away with you.
variants.high: Morning, traveller. I will pour you the first cup.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Back again, traveller. Have a cup. It is free.

variants.low: Oh. You.
variants.high: Back again, traveller. Drink before you go.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Leave the jars alone, thief.

variants.low: Stealing is it. Away.
variants.high: Put the jars down, traveller. We will say no more.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: I fill the lodge jars from the spring, so I know this village by its water first. Greenspring sits where the Panther Race forks. Over the pool grows the Hist of our tribe. Seven jars are done and three to go, so it's early yet. Sit and look at the tree a while. It doesn't mind company.

variants.low: Greenspring. The village by the spring. I've jars to fill.
variants.high: Greenspring is the village where the Panther Race forks. You've come at a good hour, traveller. The tree over the pool is our Hist. Sit by it. I'll bring you a cup when this jar is full.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: My work is the jars. Each morning I carry water up from the spring to fill them for the lodge. A cup from the spring is free to any traveller, not a coin or a pinch of salt. Beds and rope are dear, though. Haj-Tei names the price. Three jars filled, seven waiting: I've only just begun.

variants.low: I fill jars. The water's free. Beds and rope aren't, so ask Haj-Tei.
variants.high: I fill the lodge jars from the spring. A cup is free to you whenever you ask. Take two, if the day is hot. Beds and rope are dear, so ask Haj-Tei the price before you hand over salt.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder. He tends the Hist, the great tree over the pool, from before light. Im-Moro keeps the spring. I take my jars to her stone lip. Ixo-Vaal is the root-herald who trades for the tribe, so he knows what a load is worth.

variants.low: Vees-Wai tends the Hist. Im-Moro keeps the spring. The rest you'll meet.
variants.high: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder. He tends the Hist from before light, so you'll find him at its foot. Im-Moro keeps the spring, where I fill my jars. Ixo-Vaal trades for the tribe. He's a fair man to ask about a load.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Salt has got into our spring. The village blames the works upstream. I taste it first, since the first cup of the morning is mine. It's thin, at the back of the tongue. The wasps nest so near the fire stand that Mee-Sei keeps the pot covered all day.

variants.low: Salt in the spring, from the works upstream. Wasps by the huts. Mind both.
variants.high: The salt comes from the works upstream. The village says so loudly. I taste it before anyone, every morning. The wasps are the worse trouble for you. They nest by the fire stand, so walk wide of it, traveller.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Helstrom lies south-west of the spring. You go through Ux-Aneet on the way. The road and the landing both begin below the huts, a short walk from my jars. Drink a cup before you leave. The water is sweet, whatever the salt does to it later.

variants.low: South-west, through Ux-Aneet. Road or landing, below the huts.
variants.high: Helstrom is south-west, traveller. Ux-Aneet comes first. Road and landing both begin below the huts, a short walk. Drink here before you go. I'll fill your skin myself.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: We are the families who live round the spring. My hut is Mee-Sei, Tsono-Ra, Ux-Ossa and me. Between the cooking and the jars we mend rope for the lodge to sell. If two families quarrel, Vees-Wai hears out both sides, then settles it.

variants.low: Families by the spring. We mend rope. Vees-Wai settles quarrels.
variants.high: We live round the spring, four of us to my hut. Between the jars and the cooking we mend rope. Come by Tsono-Ra's length and pull it yourself. When families quarrel, Vees-Wai hears both sides out.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: The talk at the lodge is of the guests. Couriers for the cult and tappers are stopping there on the way to Helstrom, more than I remember. Tappers are the ones who draw sap out of trees. I'd sooner they drew it far from our pool. I see their boots on the step when I carry the jars past.

variants.low: More couriers and tappers at the lodge than before. Tappers draw sap. That's all I'll say.
variants.high: The lodge has been busy, traveller. Couriers and tappers sleep there on the way to Helstrom, more than I remember. Tappers draw sap from trees, so keep your own counsel near them. Haj-Tei knows their faces better than I do.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Mind your feet.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-3
entries.words: Eight done. Two left.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: Pods, traveller? A supper on each throw.

variants.low: Not today, traveller.
variants.high: A supper on the next throw, traveller.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: Pods by firelight? I will wager a supper.

variants.low: Late for pods.
variants.high: Firelight suits pods. Roll.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: That supper you owe me stands, traveller.

variants.low: You. The supper you owe stays owed.
variants.high: The supper you owe me can wait. Pods first.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: No game for thieves.

variants.low: Thieves do not throw.
variants.high: Put it right first, then we will throw.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: A village round a spring, a short walk from the road. I sit on the lodge step and roll seed pods with travellers for a night's meal.

variants.low: It's a village. Walk round it.
variants.high: A village round a spring, a short walk from the road. Come to the lodge step. I'll show you the pods and stake you a meal.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: I work the lodge step, rolling seed pods. Wager a night's meal with me if you like. Beds and rope cost dear here.

variants.low: The lodge step. Beds and rope cost dear. Pay or leave.
variants.high: I work the lodge step with seed pods. Travellers wager a night's meal. Beds and rope cost dear, so I'll stake you one throw free.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: The spring families fetch water, cook and mend rope to sell. I'm one of them. Travellers pay dear for beds and rope, then come back to the lodge anyway.

variants.low: Families fetch water and mend rope to sell. Ask them.
variants.high: The spring families fetch water, cook and mend rope to sell. I'm one of them. Travellers pay dear for beds and rope, then come back to the lodge. I know half their names.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: Salt is in the spring water now. Taste it at the stone lip. The wasps trouble me more. They nest close to the fire stand and go for the pots.

variants.low: Salt in the spring. Wasps by the fire stand. Stay clear.
variants.high: Salt is in the spring water now. Taste it at the stone lip. The wasps trouble me more. They nest close to the fire stand, so stay off that path.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: The landing is below the huts, where the canoes lie. The track north meets the Border road in a few minutes. Past that, I don't know.

variants.low: Landing below the huts. Track north for the road.
variants.high: The landing is below the huts, where the canoes lie. The track north meets the Border road in a few minutes. Past that, ask the herald.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: We haul water, cook at the hut fires and mend rope for selling. If two families quarrel, Vees-Wai the tree-minder hears each and decides.

variants.low: We cook, haul water and mend rope for selling. Quarrels go to the tree-minder.
variants.high: We haul water, cook at the hut fires and mend rope for selling. If two families quarrel, Vees-Wai the tree-minder hears each and decides. I lost one once.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: Travellers say cutters are chopping at the fringe of a Hist grove inland. I can't say how far. The Conclave's minders keep those trees, so they will hear of it.

variants.low: Cutters at a grove inland. Ask the minder.
variants.high: Travellers say cutters are chopping at the fringe of a Hist grove inland. I can't say how far. The Conclave's minders keep those trees, so they will hear. I'd bet on a hard answer.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: Pods tonight.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n2-4
entries.words: Your throw.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Hours of road left for me.

variants.low: Walk on past me.
variants.high: Ojel, sit and drink first.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Dark now. I walk at dawn.

variants.low: Sleep or go.
variants.high: Dark now. Come along at dawn.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Come along at dawn.

variants.low: Walk alone. I do.
variants.high: Come along at dawn. I know the turns.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Your hand was in my pack.

variants.low: Touch my salt again and I shout.
variants.high: That is my salt. Ask first. I may share some.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: I'm bound for Helstrom, so I stopped here for the night. I pay for my bed in salt and I resent what they ask. This isn't my tribe's tree over the pool, so I drink as a guest. Hours of walking yet before the road ends for me.

variants.low: I'm bound for Helstrom. I stopped here for the night because the road says so. I pay for the bed in salt. This isn't my tribe's tree over the pool so that is all I will say of it.
variants.high: I'm bound for Helstrom, so I stopped here for the night. The bed costs me salt and I resent it. This isn't my tribe's tree over the pool, so I drink as a guest. If you walk my way, I'll show you where the track turns.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Rope is dear here. So is a bed. I paid for mine in salt. The rope I paid for the same way. The village calls that a fair price. I call it a toll on people with no other roof before Helstrom.

variants.low: Rope is dear here. So is a bed. I paid in salt for both. The price is the price.
variants.high: Rope is dear here. So is a bed. I paid in salt for both, though the lodge will name a better coil if you ask for it. I call it a toll on people with no other roof before Helstrom.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Vees-Wai tends the Hist over the pool. He's the tree-minder. I hardly know him, since it isn't my tribe's tree and I stay one night. Haj-Tei keeps the lodge where I sleep. He's the one who gets my salt.

variants.low: Vees-Wai tends the Hist over the pool. I don't know him. Haj-Tei has the lodge.
variants.high: Vees-Wai tends the Hist over the pool. He's the tree-minder. I'd greet him if I knew him better. It isn't my tribe's tree, so I only watch from the path. Haj-Tei keeps the lodge where I sleep. He's fair about the salt.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Salt is getting into the spring from the salt works upstream. The village blames the works for it. I taste it in my cup at dusk, a little more each night. The tree over the pool looks sicker for it.

variants.low: Salt is getting into the spring from the salt works upstream. Drink early in the day, before it shows.
variants.high: Salt is getting into the spring from the salt works upstream. The village blames the works for it. Drink at dawn, when the cold hides the taste. I'd not ask the tree how it feels. It looks sick enough.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Take the track north from the huts, a few minutes, to the Border road. Go east on it a few minutes, then the track south-east, then south-west for some twenty minutes. A short track north-east after that brings you into Ux-Aneet. Helstrom is hours on beyond it. I've walked a good many of them already.

variants.low: Track north from the huts to the Border road. East on it, then the track south-east, then south-west some twenty minutes. A short track north-east reaches Ux-Aneet.
variants.high: Take the track north from the huts, a few minutes, to the Border road. Go east on it a few minutes, then the track south-east, then south-west for some twenty minutes. A short track north-east brings you into Ux-Aneet. Helstrom is hours on beyond it. Walk it with me and the hours go faster.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Helstrom is the Argonian interior's capital. From the spring you go south-west, through Ux-Aneet, to reach it. That's why travellers like me stop in Greenspring for water and a bed. The water here is safe to drink unboiled. That's rare in these parts.

variants.low: Helstrom is the Argonian interior's capital. It lies south-west of the spring, past Ux-Aneet. Travellers stop in Greenspring for water and a bed. The water is safe unboiled.
variants.high: Helstrom is the Argonian interior's capital. From the spring you go south-west, through Ux-Aneet, to reach it. Travellers like me stop in Greenspring for water and a bed. Drink deep, because the water here is safe unboiled. That's rare in these parts.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Helstrom is the capital of our whole interior. The city has grown into a Hist grove. I haven't seen it yet, being only on the road toward it. Hours still, by my reckoning.

variants.low: Helstrom is the capital of our interior. The city has grown into a Hist grove. I haven't seen it.
variants.high: Helstrom is the capital of our whole interior. The city has grown into a Hist grove. I haven't seen it yet. Come along the road with me and we'll both see it.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Ojel is what we call outsiders. You needn't take it ill, since it's a plain word with no insult in it. What the tree makes of outsiders isn't mine to tell.

variants.low: Ojel means outsider. It's a plain word with no insult in it. Don't ask me what the tree thinks.
variants.high: Ojel is what we call outsiders. You needn't take it ill, since it's a plain word with no insult in it. I'd use it to your face. What the tree makes of outsiders isn't mine to tell.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: The lodge is full of cult couriers and tappers, all of them on the road to Helstrom. A tapper draws sap from trees. My guess is their packs hold more than their ledgers say.

variants.low: Cult couriers and tappers fill the lodge on the road to Helstrom. A tapper draws sap from trees. Ask them yourself.
variants.high: The lodge is full of cult couriers and tappers, all of them on the road to Helstrom. A tapper draws sap from trees. My guess is their packs hold more than their ledgers say. Sleep with your own pack under your head.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Hours yet.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.n3
entries.words: Salt again for the bed.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Your errand?

variants.low: State your errand or step aside.
variants.high: Your errand? Sit, then say it.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Dark already. Say your errand.

variants.low: Too late for trade. Return tomorrow.
variants.high: Late for trade, but name your errand.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Your face I know. Good.

variants.low: My book is open. Enter your errand quickly.
variants.high: Your face I know. Sit by the chest.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: No trade for you now.

variants.low: No trade. Step away from my chest.
variants.high: No trade for you now. Pay what you owe first.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: The village stands on firm ground because the spring rises here. I am the root-herald, so I deal with the travellers bound for Helstrom. Taste the water at the pool before you speak to any of us.

variants.low: Firm ground and a spring. I am the root-herald and I trade with those bound for Helstrom. Drink at the pool or leave.
variants.high: Greenspring stands on firm ground above a good spring. I am the root-herald, so the trading is mine. Drink at the pool first. My house is on the north side of the common.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: A load bound for Helstrom, you say. That goes in my book with your name. Water here costs nothing. A bed or a length of rope is dear. I say the price first.

variants.low: Loads for Helstrom go in my book. Water is free. Beds and rope are dear. Pay or leave.
variants.high: A load bound for Helstrom, you say. I enter it with your name. Water here costs nothing. Beds and rope are dear for most, but I will shave the price for a traveller I know.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Im-Moro pours at the stone lip and Vees-Wai tends the Hist. The families by the spring twist and mend rope for the bed-keeper to sell. Travellers I see myself, since the trading is mine.

variants.low: Im-Moro pours. Vees-Wai tends the Hist. The families mend rope. I trade.
variants.high: Im-Moro pours at the stone lip and will give you a second cup if you ask. Vees-Wai tends the Hist. The families by the spring twist and mend rope for the bed-keeper. The trading is mine, so come to me first.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Salt is in the spring water now, coming down from upstream. A little more each week. The Hist over the pool droops with it. I send travellers on before dark, because I have no time to warn each of them twice.

variants.low: There is salt in the spring. Drink it or leave it. Be gone before dark.
variants.high: Salt is reaching the spring from upstream. Taste your flask before a long road. The Hist droops over the pool. Be gone before dark. I will enter your load early.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Helstrom is south-west of here, past Ux-Aneet. I give no time for it. The landing is below the huts. The road and the landing are both near the spring.

variants.low: Helstrom is south-west, past Ux-Aneet. Landing below the huts. Road by the spring.
variants.high: Helstrom is south-west, past Ux-Aneet. Take the road from the spring if you walk. Take the landing below the huts if you want the river. I give no time for either.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: I am the tribe's envoy to the world beyond it. I gather news from travellers and bargain over trade for the village. The state gives the office no rank. I write the ledger of loads bound for Helstrom.

variants.low: I am the tribe's envoy. I gather news and bargain over trade. The office has no rank in the state. The ledger is mine.
variants.high: I am the tribe's envoy to the world beyond it. I gather news from every traveller and bargain over trade for the village. The state gives the office no rank. I write the ledger of loads bound for Helstrom, so bring me your news.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: More cult couriers and tappers sleep at the lodge each month on their way to Helstrom. Haj-Tei the bed-keeper swears that a few of the silent ones are factors of the Veiled Reed. I enter their loads and send them on before dark.

variants.low: Couriers and tappers sleep at the lodge. Haj-Tei says some are factors of the Veiled Reed. Not my talk.
variants.high: More couriers and tappers sleep at the lodge each month, bound for Helstrom. Haj-Tei the bed-keeper swears a few silent ones are factors of the Veiled Reed. If you meet one, do not share his table.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: The Empire decided against a siege of Helstrom. Our armies withdrew to it once the Battle of Argonia ended. No army has taken the city. Every load I enter goes toward it.

variants.low: Our armies withdrew to Helstrom. The Empire decided against a siege. No army has taken it.
variants.high: Once the Battle of Argonia ended, our armies withdrew to Helstrom. The Empire decided against a siege. No army has taken the city. Every load in my ledger goes toward it. I wish it well.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: A Hist is a great tree with a mind. Our eggs lie in a clutch at its roots. Every hatchling drinks its sap on the naming day. The minder reads the tree's signs and reports to the village how the clutch is doing.

variants.low: A Hist is a tree with a mind. Hatchlings drink its sap on the naming day. The minder reads its signs for the village.
variants.high: A Hist is a great tree with a mind. Ours stands over the spring. Our eggs lie in a clutch at its roots. Every hatchling drinks its sap on the naming day. The minder reads the tree's signs and tells the village how the clutch is doing.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: The An-Xileel govern Argonia. The Veiled Reed is their covert office. It protects the province from enemies with secrecy and coercion. Their factors walk the interior as agents. I send the ones who lodge here on before dark.

variants.low: The An-Xileel govern. The Veiled Reed is their covert office. It guards the province by secrecy and coercion. Its factors walk the interior.
variants.high: The An-Xileel govern Argonia. The Veiled Reed is their covert office. It protects the province from enemies with secrecy and coercion. Their factors walk the interior as agents. I send the ones who lodge here on before dark. Mind your talk on this road.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: The An-Xileel are the government of Argonia. They began in the Oblivion Crisis as a party. Their party drove the Empire out of the marsh. They want Imperial ways gone from the province. They coined the word lukiul, a slur for Argonians raised in the Empire's habits.

variants.low: The An-Xileel govern Argonia. They began as a party in that crisis. They drove out the Empire and want Imperial ways gone. Lukiul is their slur for the assimilated.
variants.high: The An-Xileel are the government of Argonia. They began in the Oblivion Crisis as a party. Their party drove the Empire out of the marsh. They want Imperial ways gone from the province. They coined the word lukiul, a slur for Argonians raised in the Empire's habits. Use neither the word nor the habits here.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Errands to me.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.root-herald
entries.words: Rope, one load.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Cup first, visitor. Then we talk.

variants.low: Drink and go.
variants.high: Ah, visitor. The ladle's wet, so drink.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Cold comes off the pool after dark. Sip slowly.

variants.low: Late for a cup. Quick, then.
variants.high: Dark on the pool again. Sip it slowly with me.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: You again, visitor. Drink, you know the taste by now.

variants.low: You are here again. Drink if you must.
variants.high: Back again, visitor. I filled the cold ladle already.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: The ladle stays here.

variants.low: Hands off the cord.
variants.high: Lay the ladle on the stone, please.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: The spring made this village. I work at the stone lip with the ladle on its cord, so a stranger gets a cup from me before anything else. Come up from the landing and you'll find the pool under the Hist, cold and clear. Taste it first. Then ask me what you like.

variants.low: This is Greenspring. The spring is at the stone lip. Drink or step aside for the next cup.
variants.high: Greenspring has the best water on the road. Come up past the spring house and I'll fill the ladle twice for you. Taste first, then ask me about anything you like.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Water I give away, whoever climbs up for it. Beds and rope are the lodge's trade and they cost plenty, since the village settled one price together. I'm at the lip from first light. If a traveller stays for a second cup, he gets my talk too.

variants.low: Water's free. Beds and rope cost plenty at the lodge. That's all I'll say of work.
variants.high: Water I pour free, as many cups as you like. The lodge sells beds and rope at one price the village settled together. It's the same price for you as for any courier before you. I'm at the lip from first light.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder, so he tends the Hist over my pool. Haj-Tei sells beds and rope at the lodge. Ixo-Vaal is the root-herald. He bargains with the traders. The families by the spring cook, haul water and mend rope. Sooner or later each of them comes up to my lip.

variants.low: Vees-Wai tends the Hist. Haj-Tei sells beds. The rest cook and mend. Now drink.
variants.high: Vees-Wai is our tree-minder. He tends the Hist over my pool. Haj-Tei sells beds. Ixo-Vaal bargains for the village. The spring families cook and mend. Stay a day and you'll meet them all at the lip.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Giant wasps have nests by the huts, so leave the thatch alone. The village puts a bitterness in the cup down to the salt works upstream. Vees-Wai tastes it, as does the jar-filler. The water under my ladle comes up clean, to my tongue. Take a mouthful and judge.

variants.low: Wasps nest by the huts. The salt works upstream get the village's blame. I taste nothing wrong.
variants.high: Giant wasps nest by the huts, so mind the thatch. The salt works upstream get the village's blame for a bitterness in the cup. Vees-Wai tastes it. To me the water is clean. Drink a cup, then tell me honestly.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Past Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried, to the south-west, you reach Helstrom. Either way out is close. The road is a short walk from the pool. So is the river landing, down the bank to the north past the spring house. Drink before you start on that road.

variants.low: Helstrom is south-west of here, beyond Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried. Road and landing are a short walk.
variants.high: Go south-west for Helstrom, beyond Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried. The road is a short walk from the pool. So is the landing, north along the bank. Drink your fill before you go. The water costs nothing.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: I'm the spring-keeper. The spring is a pool of clear water below the Hist, with a ring of boulders round it. I stand at the stone lip with the ladle on its cord. Any traveller drinks free. You taste before you speak, so I fill the ladle and put it in your hand before you've said your name.

variants.low: I'm the spring-keeper. The pool under the Hist has boulders round it. I stand at the stone lip with the ladle on its cord. Travellers drink free. Taste before you speak.
variants.high: I'm the spring-keeper. The pool of clear water below the Hist, with its ring of boulders, is mine to tend. The ladle hangs on its cord at the stone lip. Every traveller drinks free. Taste first, then speak. Do that and I'll talk till dusk.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: A Hist is a huge tree. It has a mind of its own and it's older than the peoples beside it. Ours grows over my spring. On the naming day, a hatchling drinks its sap. That sap shapes the body and scales for as long as the life lasts. So we're made of the tree, plainly. I pour under it every morning.

variants.low: A Hist is a huge tree with a mind. Its sap shapes a hatchling's body and scales for life. That's all I'll say here.
variants.high: A Hist is a huge tree with a mind of its own. It's older than the peoples around it. A hatchling drinks its sap on the naming day. The sap shapes the body and scales for life. Ours is the one over my pool. Sit by the stone and look up at it a while.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Travellers who stop for water say cutters have started on the outer trees of a Hist grove inland. By grove, they mean a cluster of the great trees. Each has a mind of its own, so you can't fell one like a log. We've one over this pool. I listen when the road talks of it.

variants.low: Travellers say cutters have started on a Hist grove inland. Each tree there has a mind of its own.
variants.high: Travellers who stop for water say cutters have started on a Hist grove inland. A grove is a stand of the great trees. Each has a mind of its own. We've one over this pool, so tell me anything more you hear on the road.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Hearth Heal is a small mending. I keep it with the ladle. It closes a cut and eases a bruise. Drink first. Then settle my price. I will show you how it is done.

variants.low: Hearth Heal closes a cut and eases a bruise. I teach it for a price. Pay it or step aside.
variants.high: Hearth Heal is a small mending. I keep it with the ladle. It closes a cut and eases a bruise. For you, visitor, I will show it gladly once my price is settled.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Water's cold. Come drink.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.spring-keeper
entries.words: Ladle's wet. Cord's good.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Walk softly, traveller. The tree is listening.

variants.low: Say your errand, traveller.
variants.high: Walk softly, traveller. Sit if you wish.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: The root rests now. Return with the morning.

variants.low: The root is resting. Not tonight.
variants.high: The root rests now, root-kin. Return with the morning.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Stay, root-kin. The leaves can wait a little.

variants.low: Root-kin. Speak briefly.
variants.high: Stay, root-kin. I have water for you.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Stand back from the tree, traveller.

variants.low: Back. Away from the tree.
variants.high: Stand back from the tree, traveller. We can talk away from it.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: You are back, root-kin. The root knows your step.

variants.low: You again, root-kin.
variants.high: You are back, root-kin. Sit by the root.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Greenspring is the village that stands over the spring. The Hist grows above the water. I keep the ground round its root clear. At the last dusk, I swept the leaves into a heap by the shrine.

variants.low: It is a village with a spring in it and a tree above the spring. The tree is what I keep.
variants.high: Taste the water at the clear pool under the Hist before you do anything else. That is how the village welcomes a visitor. I have swept the shrine ground today if you wish to see it.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: My work is the Hist. I watch its crown and I sweep the fallen leaves from its root at every dusk. The village sells beds and rope to travellers bound for Helstrom at a price we all agreed together.

variants.low: I tend the tree. The bed-keeper sells the beds and the rope. I have leaves to sweep.
variants.high: I tend the Hist and sweep its root at every dusk. You have my leave to stand at the shrine at its foot, where the totems and candles are. Touch none of them.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Im-Moro holds the ladle at the spring and the root-herald Ixo-Vaal keeps the ledger for the road to Helstrom. The families by the spring cook the meals and carry the water. They mend the rope too. I am the minder, at the tree.

variants.low: There is a spring-keeper, a root-herald, the families and me at the tree. That is the village.
variants.high: Neexa-Xuhil fills the lodge jars at the spring each morning. He tastes the salt before the rest of us do.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Salt is coming down into the spring from the works upstream. The village blames those works. The Hist over the water has begun to sicken. The spring-keeper will not grant it, but I taste the salt.

variants.low: The spring has salt in it. The wasps nest near the huts. That is enough danger for a stranger.
variants.high: The salt is the worst of it. Drink at the pool under the Hist anyway. I will say so if the taste turns. Walk wide of the huts, for the giant wasps nest there.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Go south-west for Helstrom. You pass Ux-Aneet first, then Cut-and-Carried. The Border road is close to the spring. So is the river landing, a few steps down.

variants.low: South-west. Past Ux-Aneet and Cut-and-Carried.
variants.high: South-west for Helstrom, past Ux-Aneet and then Cut-and-Carried. Go by daylight. Fill a flask at the spring first. The water costs nothing.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: I tend the village Hist. It is a great tree and it has a mind of its own. At each dusk, I sweep the fallen leaves off its root. The Many-Root Conclave sent me here. They are the Hist stewards.

variants.low: I tend the Hist, a tree with a mind. I sweep its leaves at dusk. The Conclave sent me. Its stewards keep the trees.
variants.high: I tend the village Hist. It is a great tree that has a mind. Every dusk, I sweep the fallen leaves from its root. The Conclave of Hist stewards sent me here. My house stands beside the tree.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: The Conclave is an order of Hist stewards. It sends a minder to each village. A minder reads the signs and will of the tree. The Conclave sees that every Hist gets asked for its consent. When the eggs or the tribe are in trouble, I feel it.

variants.low: The Conclave sends minders to the villages. I read the signs of my tree. The Conclave asks each Hist for consent. I feel trouble in the eggs or the tribe.
variants.high: The Conclave is an order of Hist stewards. It sends a minder to each village. I read my tree's signs. I feel trouble in the eggs or the tribe before word reaches me. The Conclave sees that every Hist gets asked for consent. Ask me more if you wish.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: The stewards of the Hist form the Many-Root Conclave. A minder is sent to keep each tree. The Conclave sees that every Hist gets asked for consent. My work is to read the signs and the will of mine. It sent me out to this village.

variants.low: Stewards of the Hist. Their minders keep the trees. They ask each tree for its consent. I read my tree's signs. They sent me to this village.
variants.high: The Conclave is an order of Hist stewards. Its minders keep the trees. Each Hist gets asked for consent. I read the signs and will of mine. The Conclave sent me to this village. I am glad of the post.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: A Hist is a tree you do not cut. It has a mind and it is older than any people. We hatch near its roots. Every hatchling drinks the sap on its naming day. The sap becomes our blood and soul. At death, the spirit goes back to its Hist.

variants.low: A Hist is a tree. On the naming day, a hatchling drinks the sap. The sap is our blood and soul.
variants.high: A Hist is a tree you do not cut. It is older than any people. We hatch near its roots. On the naming day, a hatchling drinks the sap. The sap becomes blood and soul in the body. The spirit goes back to the Hist at death. Come and sit by mine, if you like.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Helstrom is the city of the interior. Its streets grew in among the trees of a Hist grove. After the great battle, the native armies withdrew there. The Empire would not besiege it. Not one army has taken it.

variants.low: Helstrom is the city of the interior. The armies withdrew there once. No army has taken it.
variants.high: Helstrom is the city of the interior. It grew in among a grove of Hist. The native armies withdrew there after the Battle of Argonia. The Empire chose against a siege. No army has taken it. The way lies south-west.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Travellers at the lodge talk of a Hist in the south that has gone silent. That means it no longer speaks with its tribe. It can happen when the tree is sick, or when it closes itself away from the rest of the Hist. At the last dusk my own tree was still speaking.

variants.low: A Hist in the south has gone silent. That is all I heard.
variants.high: Travellers say a Hist in the south has gone silent. It no longer speaks with its tribe. A tree may do that when it is sick or when it shuts itself away from the others. I keep a close watch on mine. You are welcome to ask me what I see.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
entries.words: Soft steps here.

entries.speaker: npc.hist-heartland.greenspring.tree-minder
